TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Ambiguity Levels on Response Strategy Transferability
PROPOSAL: Assess whether the effectiveness of an uncertainty-guided response strategy to handle ambiguity in visual questions can transfer across different ambiguity levels. This is achieved through fine-tuning a pre-trained VLM model on a large-scale synthetic dataset with varying degrees of ambiguity. 
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the fine-tuned model on validation sets with different, moderate, high, and low ambiguity levels with the base case (pre-trained model without fine-tuning). 
COST: 48 GPU-hours

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Towards Effective Clarification: A Study on Model Preferences for Clarifying Follow-Up Questions
PROPOSAL: Analyze the preferences of a pre-trained VLM model when designing a follow-up question strategy for ambiguous visual questions, focusing on the characteristics of the query and its potential impact on the model's answer uncertainty. Utilize a synthetic dataset (annotated follow-ups and query characteristics) to train a neural network that predicts follow-up questions and investigate which factors influence the success of the model.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the follow-up prediction model with a baseline that always generates follow-up questions seeking confirmation of the initial query. 
COST: 32 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model will likely identify preferences for follow-up questions that directly address ambiguity sources and may capture subtle interactions between query characteristics and model uncertainty, indicating a positive outcome for the follow-up strategy.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Towards Effective Clarification: A Study on Model Preferences for Clarifying Follow-Up Questions
PROPOSAL: Refine the previous proposal by incorporating multi-response options for ambiguous visual questions, allowing the model to produce multiple possible answers rather than a single follow-up question. Analyze how the model's answer uncertainty affects the diversity and accuracy of its response options. Utilize a synthetic dataset (annotated follow-ups and query characteristics) to evaluate the performance of the model.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the reframed model with a standard single-response model and a control that always generates plausible but semantically inadequate responses. 
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised model is expected to produce more accurate and diverse response options for ambiguous visual questions, reflecting real-world human behavior in uncertain situations, and will handle higher ambiguity levels better.

TITLE: Analysis of AQALib: A Library for Ambiguity Levels in Visual Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive library, AQALib, consisting of a predefined set of synthetic visual question answering tasks, each with its own level of ambiguity, covering various scenarios of ambiguities such as semantic ambiguity, linguistic ambiguity, image ambiguity, and spatial ambiguity. Utilize this library to create a benchmark for evaluating the performance of models on ambiguous visual question answering tasks, facilitating or comparing model performances across different styles of ambiguity.
CONTROLS: Measure the performance of the library against a diverse set of state-of-the-art models, and examine whether the models can differentiate between different ambiguity levels and respond accordingly. 
COST: 56 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The library will become a universally accepted benchmark for open questions and approaches, providing a standardized tool for the research community to evaluate, compare, and distinguish between AI's various ambiguity levels in visual question answering.

TITLE: Adaptive Response Strategy for Ambiguous Visual Questions using Bayesian Active Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop an adaptive response strategy for ambiguous visual questions that combines uncertainty estimates with active learning principles. Using Bayesian active learning, the model actively selects follow-up questions to clarify ambiguity and update its uncertainty estimates. Assess the effectiveness of this approach in reducing ambiguity and improving response accuracy on the AQALib benchmark.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the adaptive response strategy against the uncertainty estimation framework (revised in turn 7) and the standard baseline model on AQALib benchmark. 
COST: 64 GPU-hours

TITLE: Exposing Communication Breakdown in Ambiguous Visual Question Answering: A Multi-Modal Evaluation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the breakdown of communication between humans and AI systems in ambiguous visual question answering scenarios. Utilize a multi-modal evaluation framework that integrates natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, and human-in-the-loop evaluations to assess the performance of AI systems in handling ambiguity. Evaluate the effects of different response strategies, including the adaptive strategy proposed in turn 8, on communication breakdown and human satisfaction.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the adaptive response strategy against the uncertainty estimation framework and the standard baseline model on the multi-modal evaluation framework. 
COST: 96 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The multi-modal evaluation will expose the patterns of communication breakdown and provide valuable insights into the human-AI interaction dynamics, which will help refine the adaptive response strategy and improve the overall human-AI communication in ambiguous visual question answering scenarios.

TITLE: Framework for Assessing and Improving Human-AI Cooperation in Ambiguous Visual Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Synthesize the findings from previous experiments and evaluation studies to develop a comprehensive framework for assessing and improving human-AI cooperation in ambiguous visual question answering scenarios. The framework will incorporate insights from cognitive science, human-computer interaction, and AI research to provide a structured approach for evaluating and enhancing the human-AI interaction in various complexity levels. The framework will serve as a foundation for future development of more robust and cooperative AI systems.
CONTROLS: Utilize the AQALib benchmark and the multi-modal evaluation framework to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. 
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The framework is expected to significantly improve human-AI cooperation in ambiguous visual question answering scenarios, enhancing the overall user experience and usability of AI systems, and providing a foundation for the development of more advanced and cooperative AI technologies.

TITLE: Investigating Ambiguity Types in Visual Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Develop a systematic categorization of ambiguity types in visual questions based on contextual and question-focused features using a test set of 10,000 synthetic images and 50 question types. Compare the ranking of ambiguity types using metrics such as human answer complexity, question type, and query-ability. Select and evaluate top performing feature combinations for later use in strategy adaptation.
CONTROLS: Human evaluation of ambiguity, standard VQA metrics.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed categorization system will identify 5 distinct ambiguity types, primarily influenced by question type and contextual features. Validation will show that the top-ranking features are domain-independent and applicable across various VQA benchmarks.

Note: This proposal establishes a foundation for assessing ambiguity in VQA, which will later inform strategy adaptation and evaluation.

TITLE: Evaluating Strategic Adaptation of VLMs in Ambiguous Visual Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Adapt the pipeline from Proposal 1 to train and evaluate a visual question answering model equipping it with 4 context-appropriate response strategies (answer, infer, list alternatives, clarify) based on ambiguity type and question difficulty. Use a benchmark consisting of 5K synthetic VQA pairs with officially annotated ambiguity and difficulty levels. Compare this adaptable model to a baseline answering system that always follows the ask clarification strategy or responds with confidence.
CONTROLS: Baseline answering model, VLM models with standard VQA metrics, adaptive VLM model without strategy adaptation.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results will show that adaptation outperforms both baselines and that the list alternative strategy significantly improves performance for high ambiguity types. We anticipate to see a correlation between model performance and ambiguity stratification accuracy from Proposal 1.

ACTION: REVISE 2

PROPOSAL: Modify Proposal 2 to include a set of pre-defined follow-up questions to test the model's ability to clarify and adapt to ambiguity. For instance, if the model responds with "what is the brand", a follow-up question "which brand is red" would reveal whether it can refine its answer based on subsequent queries. Additionally, validate the generalization of the model by fine-tuning the adaptable model on a real-world dataset (e.g. Edinburgh VQA 01).
CONTROLS: Baseline answering system, VLM models with standard VQA metrics, VLM models with strategy adaptation without pre-defined follow-ups, fine-tuned adaptable model.
COST: No change (incremental modification to existing experiment).
PREDICTION: This refinement will allow us to evaluate the effectiveness of the adaptable model in real-world-like conversations. While performance improvements are expected, the model may struggle with real-world nuances, requiring further adjustments.

TITLE: Investigating the Role of Attention Mechanisms in Ambiguity Handling
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of attention mechanisms on the adaptability of visual language models to ambiguous visual questions. Design and evaluate a set of attention-based models, including self-attention, cross-attention, and query-aware attention, and compare their performance against baseline and adaptable models. PROPOSAL: Evaluate the transferability of adaptable visual language models trained on ambiguous visual question answering to other visual question answering tasks, such as image classification and captioning, and explore the effects of adaptation on ambiguity handling. Investigate the factors that determine the domain and task transferability, including similarity in question types, object presence or absence, and the linguistic complexity of questions.

COST: 600 GPU-hours
